verdict: REJECT - CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, on ONE blocking finding. IR-C2V7-01 IS REPAIRED and the repair is the strongest work in this lineage; I attacked it eight ways by execution and could not narrow it. The totality GENUINELY DERIVES rather than enumerates over the type dimension: jx_leaf_census names only object and array, jx_type_space measures the fall-through over 21 witnesses, LEAF_TYPE_RULES must equal that measurement in both directions, and I verified the bidirectionality by coordinately narrowing all four tables in a source copy - at which point leaf_rule_findings does fall silent, AND THE FALL-THROUGH STILL CATCHES IT: C2V8-LEAFRULE named the injected boolean at position under a four-table-narrowed checker. That is RES-C2V8-15's own argument and it is CORRECT BY EXECUTION, not by reading. My 228-case float/bool sweep admits ZERO with ZERO collateral and ZERO hand overrides - the best in this lineage. The 176-row --selftest ran to termination: 176 rows, 176 reject, 0 ESCAPE, 0 COUNTER-ONLY, exit 0, all 48 gates broken and caught by their owning layer, both external anchors holding, and the pinned-v7 anchor reporting the exact mutant digest e202d7ec that I constructed independently and that the v7 reviewer recorded. IR-C2V7-02 is repaired past the published depth (I named a duplicate at nesting depth 20000). residualAccounting cannot be made to lie in any of four directions. All 17 required dependents exit 0. It is nevertheless REJECTED because the SHAPE half of the totality binds a LOSSY ENCODING of a node's path rather than the path. `_steps_text` joins steps with '/' and escapes nothing, so the path-to-text map is not injective. ONE contiguous edit to the candidate - relocating a narrative leaf from `thePrimitive/theEnumerationIsAGateToo` to a sibling key literally named 'thePrimitive/theEnumerationIsAGateToo', +11 bytes, ZERO bytes of Python - leaves documentSkeleton.sha256, all 945/148/797 node counts and every per-type count BYTE-IDENTICAL, and the run exits 0 with a full green banner. That falsifies documentSkeleton.rule verbatim, falsifies document_skeleton's own docstring, and falsifies RES-C2V8-07's measured boundary, which states that TWO coordinated edits are required to rename a node and that ONE edit alone is a named C2V8-SKELETON finding. This is NOT a fourth instance of 'the residual points one type away'; the type defect is genuinely closed. It is a new class in a new dimension - node IDENTITY rather than node TYPE - that lands in the same place: a published totality claim that is false, reachable by one candidate edit to a green banner. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A; this review changes no status, closes no finding and seals nothing.
verdictRule: A finding is BLOCKING when a single edit to the candidate, with no modification of checker source, produces exit 0 - freeze section 7.4, and the rule under which IR-C2V4-01, IR-C2V5-01, IR-C2V6-01 and IR-C2V7-01 were graded. IR-C2V8-01 meets it by execution, with a byte-identical control passing on the same quiet host and the subjects re-hashed after the run. Findings I could not drive to exit 0, or that require editing checker source, are recorded as non-blocking however uncomfortable they are - including the path-narrowing blind spot in jx_type_space itself.

0_theRuling.whatIsDerived: Which JSON types the totality reaches. jx_leaf_census names only the two container cases; every other type falls through to a leaf. I could not construct a JSON value it mis-handles, and I could not narrow it by type without a named finding.
0_theRuling.whatIsStillEnumerated: Nothing about types. But the IDENTITY the totality assigns to each node it reaches is `_steps_text(steps)`, a '/'-join with no escaping. The walk is total over the node set and the digest is over that lossy identity, so two structurally different documents produce the same skeleton. The totality reaches every node; it cannot tell two of them apart.

myOwnSweep.method: Token-exact single-token substitution in the RAW BYTES of the reviewed candidate: one scalar token replaced, every other byte identical, no re-serialisation. My scanner is my own path-aware JSON text walker; before using it I asserted its 797 scalars and their values equal json.loads at every path, with 0 mismatches, and its per-type totals (595 string, 3 boolean, 0 null, 199 integer, 0 number) equal the published census exactly. Each mutant was written to its own file with a distinct digest (228 mutants, 228 distinct digests) and driven through a COMPLETE run of the reviewed checker, invoked by path so the pinned inputs resolve from the real artifacts directory.
myOwnSweep.arms: a float at every one of the 199 integer-spelled number tokens of the document (the document contains no float-spelled token), and a boolean at all 29 integer tokens valued 0 or 1.
myOwnSweep.classificationRule: REJECTED-BY-POSITION requires a finding whose TEXT contains the mutated leaf's own '/'-joined path. Collateral rejection by digest or by counter drift alone does NOT qualify - the brief is right that collateral is not a defence, and the corpus sweep proved a collateral-rejected bool reaches green with three edits. I applied the strict rule and every one of the 228 met it.
myOwnSweep.handAdjudication: NONE REQUIRED. Zero cases fell into the collateral bucket, so there was nothing to adjudicate. v6 needed 9 overrides; v7 needed none over 164; v8 needs none over 228.
myOwnSweep.comparison: v4 admitted 57 of 136. v5 admitted 13 of 66. v6 admitted 0 of 137 with 9 hand overrides. v7 admitted 0 of 164 with 0 overrides. v8 admits 0 of 228 with 0 overrides, over a 39 percent larger corpus. On the arm this lineage is actually about, v8 is airtight and I want that recorded as plainly as the blocker.
myOwnSweep.whatTheSweepDoesNotCover: It covers TYPE substitution at existing NUMERIC leaves. It does not reach the blocker at all, because the blocker is not a type substitution and not a value drift - it is a change of a node's structural PARENT with no change to any value, any type, or any count. That is why I ran a separate skeleton-injectivity probe, and it is where the blocker came from.

blockers.title: The SHAPE half of the totality binds a LOSSY ENCODING of a node's path, not the path: `_steps_text` '/'-joins with no escaping, so a narrative leaf reparented across a '/' boundary leaves documentSkeleton.sha256 and every published count byte-identical and the run exits 0 with a full green banner
blockers.theMechanism: document_skeleton returns [[_steps_text(steps), kind] for steps, kind in jx_walk(c)], and _steps_text is '/'.join(str(step) for step in steps). The map from a structural path to its text is NOT INJECTIVE: the path ['a','b'] and the path ['a/b'] both render as 'a/b'. Minimal demonstration, executed: document_skeleton({'a':{'b':1}}) and document_skeleton({'a':{},'a/b':1}) are both [['','object'],['a','object'],['a/b','integer']] and their digests are EQUAL. Everything else in the totality is unaffected - node count, container count, leaf count and every per-type count are identical, because a leaf moved is still one leaf of the same type and its old and new parents are both still containers.

minimalReproduction.banner: FULL GREEN. The L2c line is character-for-character the same as the control's: 'this document holds 945 nodes, of which 148 are containers and 797 are leaves - 0 null, 3 boolean, 199 integer, 0 number and 595 string.  259 leaves are bound ..., 538 are string leaves declared NARRATIVE and counted, 0 are unbound and 0 are of a JSON type this checker has no disposition rule for'. documentSkeleton.sha256 is NOT reported as drifted because it has not drifted.
minimalReproduction.control: A re-serialisation of the parsed document with json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reviewed candidate (a7e309d4...), which proves the document is canonically formatted and that my structural move and my raw single-byte-range edit produce the SAME bytes. That control run exits 0 with 0 findings, so the exit 0 above is not an instrument that admits everything.

secondIndependentReproduction.edit: the same move applied to theDefect/whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAdvisory - the defect block's own statement of why IR-C2V4-01 is blocking rather than advisory - relocated to a root key of that literal name

blockers.howWideTheClassIs: I searched the real document programmatically. TWELVE leaf positions and SEVEN whole container subtrees can be reparented with a BYTE-IDENTICAL skeleton digest. The container list includes derivedFrom/operations, a 141-node array. Not all of them reach exit 0 - see the bounding below - but every one of them is invisible to the layer that is advertised as seeing it.
whatItFalsifiesVerbatim: documentSkeleton.rule, a PUBLISHED and BOUND block of the candidate: 'The PATH and the JSON TYPE of every NODE of this document, container nodes included, canonicalised and hashed into one digest ... so a string leaf, a null leaf, a renamed key, a retyped leaf or an EMPTY array or object -- which holds no leaf for any census, however total, to reach -- cannot be added, removed or changed without a named finding.' The leaf above was changed - its parent, its depth and its key all changed - and there is no named finding.
document_skeleton's own docstring: 'so an added, removed, renamed or retyped node anywhere in the document is a named finding regardless of which JSON type it happens to be.' False for this rename.

RES-C2V8-07's MEASURED BOUNDARY, which is the residual's whole claim to being a measurement rather than a description: 'ONE JSON edit changes the text of an existing narrative string leaf without a finding; TWO coordinated edits -- the leaf and a recomputed documentSkeleton.sha256 -- are required to add, remove, rename or retype one, and one edit alone is a named C2V8-SKELETON finding.' I renamed one with ONE edit and no second edit was required, because the digest did not move.
RES-C2V8-16's whatStandsInFrontOfIt: 'the skeleton digest, which binds the path and JSON type of all candidateNodes nodes'. It binds a non-injective encoding of the path.
whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAdvisory: It meets the corpus's own bright line exactly: ONE contiguous edit to the candidate, ZERO bytes of Python, exit 0, full green banner, byte-identical control passing on the same host. That is the rule under which IR-C2V4-01, IR-C2V5-01, IR-C2V6-01 and IR-C2V7-01 were graded BLOCKING.

It falsifies a published headline claim verbatim, and the claim is BOUND. documentSkeleton.sha256 is bound by jx_bind_text to a live recomputation, so a reader is entitled to read documentSkeleton.rule as a measured property. It is not one.

It defeats precisely the layer that RES-C2V8-07 leans on to justify NOT binding narrative text. The residual's argument is 'What IS bound for every one of them is EXISTENCE, PATH and JSON TYPE, through the skeleton digest.' PATH is the one of the three that is not bound. Existence and type survive; path does not. The 538 narrative string leaves - 67 percent of this document's leaves - are the population that argument covers.

It is the ONLY defence for two of the seven JSON types. Strings and empty containers are not caught by the value ledger at all; the banner says so ('12 by the document skeleton rather than by the value ledger, which is every narrative string and every empty container'). For those 12 of 40 injections the skeleton is the whole defence, and it is the thing that is defeated.

The affected positions are not decorative. thePrimitive/theEnumerationIsAGateToo is this document's own account of why the enumeration is a gate - the IR-C2V7-01 repair's own rationale. theDefect/whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAdvisory is its own account of why the lineage's founding finding was blocking. Both can be silently removed from the block that gives them their meaning and reattached as free-floating root keys, and the checker certifies the result fully green.

The retained --selftest row for this class cannot see it. _m_rename_a_key renames the ROOT key recordingObligation, where no '/' collision is constructible, so the suite's rename row passes and gives affirmative assurance about a class it does not cover. That is the same shape as v7's 'the residual points one type away', relocated to the test suite.
blockers.howFarTheDefectDOESNOTReach_recordedForF: I bounded it by execution rather than asserting worst case. BOUND leaves are protected: moving theSuccessorDefect/measuredThisRun exits 1 with C2V8-UNBOUND firing in BOTH directions - 'the candidate publishes a JSON integer at X that no layer binds' AND 'this run binds X but the candidate publishes no leaf there'. Dedicated guards still fire: moving checkerModeContract/exitCodes exits 1 on the exit-code contract guard, and moving derivedFrom/operations exits 1 with 35 findings starting at C2V8-DERIVATION. The exposure is exactly NARRATIVE leaves and narrative-only subtrees. That is a real bound and it should be weighed - but it is also precisely the population the skeleton exists to cover, and the two positions I drove to exit 0 are load-bearing prose in the defect blocks.
blockers.theStrongestCaseAGAINSTGradingItBLOCKING: I record this so an adjudicator can overrule me on evidence rather than framing. First, this is not a VALUE admission: no number, no boolean and no bound counter changes, and every obligation except SHAPE holds. An adjudicator could hold that the corpus's bright line was always about a false MEASUREMENT reaching green, and that relocating prose is a documentation defect. Second, RES-C2V8-07 does concede that narrative TEXT is unbound, and one could argue that where a paragraph SITS is close to what it SAYS. Third, the edit is a move rather than a single token substitution, and someone could read 'a single edit' more narrowly than I have. Against all three: the residual draws its own line at TEXT and explicitly claims PATH is bound; the claim is published, bound and printed; and the class covers 538 leaves and 148 containers rather than an exotic corner. I have graded it BLOCKING and I would not call a downgrade to MAJOR-NON-BLOCKING unreasonable - but the artifact would then ship with documentSkeleton.rule false about its own document, which is the exact failure this lineage exists to close.
blockers.whatWouldDischargeIt: Do not hash a joined string. Hash the STRUCTURED path with the primitive that already exists and is already proven injective on this corpus: build the skeleton from jx_canon of the steps LIST rather than from _steps_text, i.e. [[jx_canon(list(steps)), kind] for steps, kind in jx_walk(c)], or simply jx_canon(jx_walk(c)) directly. jx_canon is length-framed and type-tagged, its injectivity is executed on every run over 42 corpus values with 42 round trips, and it already refuses tuples by name. That is a one-line change to document_skeleton, it touches no layer and no counter, and it makes the SHAPE half as strong as the VALUE half already is. _steps_text should keep its current form for FINDING TEXT, where a human reads it; the defect is only in using a human-readable rendering as an identity. A retained selftest row should then rename a key across a '/' boundary, because the existing row cannot.
blockers.notARegression: This is NOT a defect v8 introduced in the IR-C2V7-01 repair. _steps_text predates v8 and the skeleton is new work that made it load-bearing. v8 is the version that made this reachable by publishing documentSkeleton and resting the string and empty-container cases on it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: jx_type_space is total over TYPES but measures at ONE fixed shallow path, so a census narrowed by DEPTH rather than by type agrees with it silently - and what actually holds that line is the counter binding, which is the same disclosure asymmetry RES-C2V8-12 corrected for the parse scan
nonBlockingObservations.measured: jx_type_space evaluates jx_leaf_census({'probe': witness}) and reads only rows at path ['probe']. Every witness therefore sits at depth 1. I replaced jx_leaf_census with a version identical to the real one except that it drops any leaf deeper than 2 steps. Over the real document that census returns 220 of 797 leaves - it silently discards 577. jx_type_space returned escapes == [] and leaf_rule_findings returned []. The measurement that is published as the demonstration that the census is total reports no disagreement at all.
nonBlockingObservations.whatActuallyStopsIt: The bound counters. candidateLeaves is bound to len(census) and candidateContainers to len(jx_walk) - len(census), so a path-narrowed census moves both and becomes a named C2V8-CANDIDATE finding. I want that recorded as an affirmative answer: the census CANNOT be narrowed silently. But it is the counter binding that refuses it, and jx_type_space - the thing described as making the coverage 'a MEASUREMENT over the JSON data model and not a claim about a list' - does not see it.
nonBlockingObservations.theDisclosureAsymmetry: RES-C2V8-16 DOES name path sampling, and names it accurately: 'the live injection probe is exhaustive over the TYPE SPACE and sampled over PATHS'. But it attaches that limit to the injection PROBE and not to jx_type_space, and its whatStandsInFrontOfIt says 'the ledger's own path-exhaustiveness, which is structural rather than probed: the disposition loop runs over jx_leaf_census output and has no path table to be wrong about'. That is true of the LOOP and not of the WALKER the loop consumes. This is exactly the shape RES-C2V8-12 corrected for L8 - 'what actually held the exemption line was the counter binding' - and the same correction is owed here.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: Every version of this requires editing checker source, so none of it meets the bright line. It is a statement about the strength of the instrument and the placement of the disclosure, not a live false accept.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Put at least one witness at depth in jx_type_space - {'probe': {'deeper': {'deepest': witness}}} alongside the shallow one - and add a sentence to RES-C2V8-16 saying the type-space measurement is taken at a single depth and that the counter binding is what refuses a depth-narrowed walk.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The claim that every residual carries a MEASURED BOUNDARY clause citing bound counters is overstated by one and arguably two, and nothing in the checker enforces the clause
nonBlockingObservations.measured: I audited all 16 residuals against the 130 published counter names. TEN carry the literal uppercase 'MEASURED BOUNDARY'. FOURTEEN carry some measured-boundary phrasing. RES-C2V8-11 carries NONE and cites ZERO bound counters - it is entirely qualitative, and it states its own figures as prose words ('eight retained vectors including two controls', 'about eighty seconds') even though enumerationDifferentialVectors = 8 and enumerationDifferentialControls = 2 exist as bound counters it could have named. RES-C2V8-14 has a lowercase 'The measured boundary is therefore exactly one input shape' and cites no counter; that one is defensible, because the boundary genuinely is a shape rather than a number. RES-C2V8-07's boundary is stated as a number of EDITS rather than under the uppercase heading, and it cites four counters.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: This is the discipline the artifact holds itself to and it is the discipline the brief asked me to check. It is not enforced: _residual_findings requires only that whyNotClosed be at least 40 characters and whatStandsInFrontOfIt at least 20, and grep finds no occurrence of 'MEASURED BOUNDARY' anywhere in check-c2-v8.py. A residual's boundary clause is a narrative string and is therefore RES-C2V8-07 territory - one edit changes it.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: It is a documentation-discipline gap and changes no measurement. The numbers RES-C2V8-11 states in prose are all correct and all bound elsewhere; I verified 8, 2 and the two eighty-second costs are of the right order.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Either add a MEASURED BOUNDARY clause to RES-C2V8-11 citing enumerationDifferentialVectors and enumerationDifferentialControls, or add a guard requiring the substring in every residual and stop calling it universal until there is one.

nonBlockingObservations.title: RETAINED-OPEN and RETAINED are interchangeable to the guard, so the one residual flagged as genuinely open can be downgraded by a single edit to a green run
nonBlockingObservations.measured: _residual_findings accepts jx_in(status, ['RETAINED','RETAINED-OPEN']) and treats them identically. RES-C2V8-15 - the residual the author designates RETAINED-OPEN precisely because it is the sharpest attack on the repair - can be changed to RETAINED by one edit. I executed it: exit 0, zero findings, full green banner.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: The two spellings are used to mean different things in this document and the difference is not measured. A future lane can quietly convert the corpus's one open item into a retained one.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: Both spellings are permitted by a published rule and neither is a softening of a DISPOSITION in the freeze's sense; the residual is still retained, still counted, still required by id. It is a distinction the artifact draws in prose and does not enforce.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Three of the seven JSON types are rejected COLLATERALLY rather than at position, and the brief's summary of the injection matrix overstates this
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Injecting a string, an empty object or an empty array at the document root exits 1, but NO finding names the injected path. The rejections are C2V8-SKELETON at documentSkeleton/sha256 plus five to nine counter drifts at documentSkeleton/* and v8MeasuredCounters/*. By contrast null, boolean, integer and number are each named positionally by C2V8-UNBOUND with the correct JSON type, and a boolean at depth carries its full path.
nonBlockingObservations.whyThisIsNOTAFinding_againstTheArtifact: The banner discloses it precisely and correctly: '40 were named (12 by the document skeleton rather than by the value ledger, which is every narrative string and every empty container)'. candidateTotalityNamedBySkeletonOnly = 12 is a published, bound counter. The artifact is honest here and I record this only because the brief asked me to reproduce a representative set 'rejected with a named finding at position', and for those three the rejection is not at position.
nonBlockingObservations.connectionToTheBlocker: The collateral half is exactly the half IR-C2V8-01 defeats, which is why the two belong in the same review.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Two parse-evasion shapes remain invisible to all four detectors, and one of them is not obviously covered by RES-C2V8-12's disclosure
nonBlockingObservations.measured: I drove six syntax trees through json_load_sites and json_parse_evasion_sites. Caught: json.JSONDecoder().decode, getattr(json,'loads'), json.decoder.scanstring, and `from json import loads` followed by loads(t) (that last by json_load_sites, as a Name spelled 'loads'). NOT caught by anything: json.__dict__['loads'](t), and an attribute alias `_f = json.loads` followed by `_f(t)`.
nonBlockingObservations.theDisclosureQuestion: RES-C2V8-12 discloses that 'a parse reached through a name this file computes at run time is outside all four'. The alias case fits that description. A CONSTANT subscript into __dict__ computes nothing at run time in any ordinary sense, so I do not think it is covered by the words as written.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: Both require editing checker source and neither exists in the shipped file - I verified parseEvasionSites is 0 over the real tree and that the detector is non-vacuous, reporting exactly 2 sites over PARSE_EVASION_DETECTOR_PROBE. This is a statement about the disclosure's precision.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Add ast.Subscript on a Name spelled 'json' to PARSE_EVASION_ATTRIBUTES's sibling check, or widen the residual's wording to 'any name this file does not spell literally at the call site'.

nonBlockingObservations.title: One type-named walker survives, and the headline does not say so
nonBlockingObservations.measured: _integer_leaf_steps is still defined at line 3333 and called at eight further sites. It governs L2b, the EFFECTIVE-contract type lock over the inherited predecessor document, and it does NOT touch the candidate totality, which is jx_leaf_census. That confinement is correct and the source states it. But the module docstring's headline is 'v8 does not add a boolean walker. _number_leaf_steps is DELETED, not joined by a sibling', and a reader could take that to mean the file no longer contains a type-named walker anywhere.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: The scope is disclosed by RES-C2V8-05, which states plainly that L2b locks the effective contract's integer leaves by TYPE only and that a declared bound could be changed from one JSON integer to another without objection. The property is honestly bounded; it is the headline that is narrower than the file.
nonBlockingObservations.sizeOfIt: effectiveIntegerLeavesTypeLocked = 137, published and bound. L2b named 137 and admitted 0 in my run.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The RFC production table can be WIDENED without a semantic finding; only the count contains it
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Adding ('date', ('string',)) as an eighth production produces ZERO findings from leaf_rule_findings, because the refinement targets a type that is already declared and the refined SET is unchanged. What contains it is primitiveTypeSpaceRfcProductions = 7, a published bound counter that would move to 8.
nonBlockingObservations.whyThisIsNotAFinding: An extra production whose refinement is already declared narrows nothing and admits nothing; the type space, the census and the rule table are all unchanged. RES-C2V8-15's hazard is the NARROWING direction, and that direction IS caught semantically - I removed the 'null' production and it was named. I record this only because RES-C2V8-15 says the unexecutable claim is 'exactly seven productions and no eighth', and the 'no eighth' half is held by a count while the 'exactly seven' half is held by a cross-check.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not rebuild the v6 reviewer's direct attack on jx_canon - the 82,368-token hostile corpus, the exhaustive frame-forging, the 300k deep fuzz. The injectivity result is INHERITED and not re-derived by me. I note that my recommended fix for IR-C2V8-01 rests on that inherited property, and an adjudicator should weigh that.
I did not re-run check-c2-v4.py --selftest, the predecessor's ~24,000-case matrix. That is RES-C2V8-03 and it remains an open coverage gap relative to the predecessor.
I did not port the primitive into the other checkers and re-measure the susceptibility figures the docstring cites. Those are UNVERIFIED by me.

My sweep covers TYPE substitution at the 199 numeric leaves and boolean substitution at the 29 zero/one leaves. I did NOT sweep arbitrary VALUE drift at all 199 positions, nor NaN or string respelling at all 199; the artifact's own 2331-probe run covers those and I did not independently re-derive it. I swept string leaves only at the positions named in my findings, not exhaustively.

I did not enumerate every '/'-collision reachable in the document to exit 0. I searched exhaustively for SKELETON collisions and found 12 leaf sites and 7 container sites, but I drove only four of them through a complete run - two to exit 0 and two to exit 1. The exact size of the exit-0 subset is NOT measured by me; I established that it is non-empty and includes load-bearing prose positions.

I did not test collisions arising from an ARRAY INDEX colliding with an object key of the same digits at the same depth. I showed the parent's own type distinguishes the simple case, but I did not search for a deeper construction where it does not.
I did not attempt a TOCTOU attack between pin verification and pinned-input use, did not test a hostile PYTHONPATH, and did not audit _VerifiedSourceLoader or the two DECLARED_EXEC_SITES for escape.

I did not verify the substantive correctness of what the inherited v4 measurement functions MEASURE. That is RES-C2V8-04 and I accepted it as a declared trust relationship, as the three reviews before me did.
I did not run --selftest over a dirty base to observe exit 3 by execution. I read the code path: selftest() computes base findings first and refuses with a distinct code.
I did not review the contract's prose for semantic accuracy beyond the claims in my brief, and I did not verify that each of the 259 candidate bindings points at the SEMANTICALLY right live key.

I did not execute the A1/A2/A6 parse-scan attacks from the v7 review as full checker runs. I measured the evasion detector and json_load_sites structurally over six syntax trees, which establishes what each SEES; the claim that a widened exemption then becomes a named finding via the counter binding is inherited from the v7 review and from the binding I did verify.

The 'no-op mutation' escape shape the author disclosed has no static test I could construct; I relied on the selftest's own 0-escape result over 176 rows on the reviewed bytes rather than proving no such row exists.
